message.content:
Based on my search, here are the main causes of incomplete bladder emptying (also known as urinary retention):

## **Obstruction or Blockage**

Physical narrowing or blockage in the urethra or bladder neck prevents urine from flowing out properly. Common causes include:

- **Enlarged prostate (BPH)** in men - the most common cause
- **Urethral stricture** - scar tissue narrowing the urethra
- **Bladder outlet obstruction**
- **Urinary tract stones** (kidney stones, bladder stones)
- **Pelvic organ prolapse** in women (cystocele, rectocele)
- **Constipation** - a full rectum can press on the bladder
- **Pelvic masses** - tumors, fibroids, or polyps
- **Tight pelvic floor muscles**

## **Nerve and Muscle Problems (Underactive Bladder)**

When the bladder muscles can't squeeze properly or the nerves controlling them are damaged:

- **Neurological conditions**: Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, stroke, Alzheimer's disease, spina bifida
- **Spinal cord injuries** or **traumatic brain injury**
- **Diabetes** - can cause diabetic neuropathy affecting bladder nerves
- **Pelvic injury** or **vaginal childbirth**
- **Weak bladder muscles** from aging, overdistention (stretched bladder), or pregnancy

## **Medications**

Certain drugs interfere with nerve signals to the bladder:
- Anticholinergics and antispasmodics
- Antidepressants
- Antihistamines and decongestants
- Opioids
- Alpha-adrenergic agonists
- Antipsychotics
- Benzodiazepines
- Calcium channel blockers

## **Other Causes**

- **Surgery** - especially pelvic surgery or anesthesia effects
- **Infections** - urinary tract infections, prostatitis, sexually transmitted diseases
- **Cauda equina syndrome** - compression of spinal nerve roots
- **Detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia** - bladder and sphincter muscles contract at wrong times

If you're experiencing incomplete bladder emptying, it's important to see a doctor because retained urine can become infected and lead to complications.

2. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/urinary-retention/symptoms-causes
3. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK538499/
4. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/15427-urinary-retention
